summary: Claude Lévi-Strauss worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the Paris Law Faculty (~1927–1931) and under Marcel Mauss (~1928–1935). He held posts at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, EHESS, and the Collège de France (1959–1982).
Claude-Auguste Court was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr and served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army.
Claudia Benthien studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg around 2005.
Claudia Weber is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit as her teacher and Gregor Ahn as her project supervisor.

Claudius Buchanan worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Cambridge (Queens' College, ~1791–1795), later serving as Vice-Provost at Fort William College in 1801.

Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg, later teaching there, at the universities of Vienna and Kiel, and at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Marburg and Deccan College under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau, among others. He held posts at the University of Marburg, University of Göttingen, and University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She held academic posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.
Clemente Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Pavia (~1899–1903) and held a post at the University of Pisa from circa 1908 to 1953.

Clinton B. Seely is an Indology scholar who held an academic appointment at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007 and attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.
Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS, University of Lyon, University of Paris, Institut de civilisation indienne, and Institut de France.

Colette Sciberras works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.

Colin Turnbull was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He completed his studies at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1946–1949), and Banaras Hindu University (~1950–1952).

Collett Cox, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Columbia, Tokyo, and Ryukoku universities under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She held a professorship at the University of Washington, attested from 1999 to 2026.
Congjun Long works in computational linguistics and Tibetology, holding posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Conor Roddy is a philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011), having studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. Educated at Thomasschule, Leipzig, and Berlin, he held posts at Leipzig (~1856–1861), Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
